destination_record.name: Kerala
destination_record.tagline: Backwater houseboats, misty tea hills and palm-fringed beaches, a short flight or an overnight train from Chennai.
destination_record.places: Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey backwaters, Kovalam, Varkala, Kumarakom, Wayanad

on.places: Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey and Kumarakom backwaters, Kochi, Kovalam, Varkala, Wayanad
on.activities: The best months for almost everything: dry, sunny days of roughly 25 to 32 degrees on the coast, and cooler air in the hills. Houseboat cruises, tea-estate walks, Periyar boat rides, beach days at Kovalam and Varkala and Wayanad treks are all at their best. Munnar and Thekkady can be chilly in December and January, and hotels and houseboats fill up around Christmas and New Year, so book early.

off.places: Munnar, Wayanad, Alleppey and Kumarakom backwaters, Thekkady, Kochi
off.activities: The south-west monsoon brings heavy rain, green hills and full waterfalls, with lower hotel rates and a good season for Ayurvedic rejuvenation. Expect rough seas at Kovalam and Varkala, so swimming is not advised, possible landslides or slow travel on hill roads, and some forest treks and viewpoints closed. Houseboat cruising can be restricted in heavy rain. Onam falls in August or September.

mid.places: Munnar, Thekkady, Wayanad, Kochi, Kovalam, Varkala
mid.activities: April and May are hot and humid on the coast at 32 to 36 degrees, so the hill stations of Munnar and Thekkady are the better choice, with pre-monsoon thunderstorms in the evenings. October is the shoulder month, with scattered showers as the north-east monsoon sets in, lighter crowds and good rates. Plan beach and houseboat days for the mornings.

profile.overview:
Kerala is a long, green strip of India's south-west coast, and few states pack so much variety into so short a distance. In a single week you can wake to mist and tea bushes in Munnar, watch boats on Periyar Lake in Thekkady, drift through the palm-lined canals of Alleppey on a houseboat and finish with a sunset on the cliffs at Varkala or the sands of Kovalam. Kochi adds its old Fort quarter, Chinese fishing nets and Kathakali, and Wayanad offers forest, caves and waterfalls.

For Chennai travellers it is one of the easiest holidays to plan: a short direct flight or an overnight train to Kochi or Thiruvananthapuram, then a private car for the whole trip. The food is generous for vegetarians, the pace is gentle and the scenery suits couples, families with children and senior parents alike. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the route around you.

facts.languages: Malayalam; English is widely understood in tourist areas, and Hindi and Tamil are understood in many places
facts.climate: Warm and humid, about 25 to 33 degrees on the coast and cooler in the hills; south-west monsoon from June to September
facts.flight_time: Chennai to Kochi or Thiruvananthapuram about 1 hr 15 min by air, or Ernakulam by overnight train in 10 to 12 hr. Delhi to Kochi about 3 hr 15 min.

reasons.title: Backwaters and houseboats
reasons.text: Stay a night on a houseboat among the canals and lakes of Alleppey and Kumarakom, with meals cooked on board.

reasons.title: Hills, tea and wildlife
reasons.text: Munnar's tea hills and Thekkady's Periyar Tiger Reserve give cool air, green views and a boat ride among the forest.

reasons.title: Beaches and cliffs
reasons.text: Kovalam and Varkala offer lighthouse views, palm-backed sand and sunsets from the cliff.

reasons.title: Culture and Ayurveda
reasons.text: Kathakali, Kalaripayattu, spice gardens and traditional Ayurvedic massage are part of everyday Kerala.

reasons.title: Close to Chennai
reasons.text: A short direct flight or an overnight train makes Kerala practical even for a long weekend.

attractions.title: Alleppey backwaters
attractions.text: A network of canals, lakes and villages best seen from a houseboat or a smaller country boat.

attractions.title: Munnar tea country
attractions.text: Rolling tea plantations, Mattupetty Dam, Echo Point and viewpoints at about 1,500 metres.

attractions.title: Eravikulam National Park
attractions.text: Grassy hills that are home to the Nilgiri tahr; the park closes for a few weeks each year for the calving season.

attractions.title: Periyar Tiger Reserve, Thekkady
attractions.text: A boat ride on Periyar Lake, with a chance to see elephants, deer and birds along the shore.

attractions.title: Fort Kochi and Mattancherry
attractions.text: Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church, Santa Cruz Basilica, Mattancherry Palace and the spice and antique lanes of Jew Town.

attractions.title: Kumarakom and Vembanad Lake
attractions.text: A quiet lakeside village with a bird sanctuary and some of the state's most relaxed resorts.

attractions.title: Kovalam and Varkala
attractions.text: Kovalam's crescent beaches and lighthouse, and Varkala's red laterite cliff above the sea.

attractions.title: Wayanad
attractions.text: Edakkal Caves, Banasura Sagar Dam, Soochipara Falls and spice-scented hills in the Western Ghats.

experiences.title: Overnight houseboat cruise
experiences.text: Cruise the backwaters by day, moor for sunset and enjoy Kerala meals prepared on board.

experiences.title: Kathakali or Kalaripayattu show
experiences.text: Watch elaborate make-up and costume or the martial art that is said to be among the oldest in India.

experiences.title: Ayurvedic massage
experiences.text: A traditional oil massage at an authorised centre is a favourite way to unwind between sightseeing days.

experiences.title: Spice plantation walk
experiences.text: See cardamom, pepper, cinnamon and vanilla growing, mostly around Thekkady and Wayanad.

experiences.title: Tea estate and sunrise views
experiences.text: Walk between the tea bushes around Munnar in the cool early morning.

experiences.title: Sunset on Varkala Cliff
experiences.text: Stroll along the cliff path and watch the sun go down over the Arabian Sea.

food.title: Kerala sadhya
food.text: A vegetarian feast of rice and many curries served on a banana leaf, especially during Onam.

food.title: Appam with vegetable stew
food.text: Lacy rice pancakes with a mild coconut-milk stew, a favourite breakfast.

food.title: Puttu and kadala curry
food.text: Steamed rice and coconut cylinders with a spiced black chickpea curry.

food.title: Seafood and coconut dishes
food.text: Fish curry, prawn roast and karimeen are specialities for those who eat non-vegetarian food.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Vegetarian food is easy to find, and we can request Jain meals with advance notice, though choices may be limited at some stops.

tips.title: Book houseboats early for peak months
tips.text: December and January fill fast. Houseboats usually cruise by day and moor for the night, and air-conditioning typically runs only at night.

tips.title: Check the weather from June to September
tips.text: Heavy monsoon rain can cause landslides and slow hill roads, close treks and make the sea unsafe for swimming.

tips.title: Swim only where it is safe
tips.text: Currents at Kovalam and Varkala can be strong. Swim near lifeguards, follow flag signs and avoid the sea in the monsoon.

tips.title: Pack for hills and humidity
tips.text: Bring light cotton for the coast and a warm layer for Munnar and Thekkady, especially from December to February.

tips.title: Dress modestly at temples
tips.text: Many Kerala temples have strict dress codes, and some admit only Hindus. Ask your driver or our team before visiting.

tips.title: Allow for slow roads
tips.text: Hill and coastal roads are winding and busy, so journeys take longer than the distance suggests. We plan days with that in mind.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa for Kerala. Carry a valid photo ID such as an Aadhaar card, passport, driving licence or voter ID for hotel check-in. No special permit is needed for the main tourist circuits, but protected areas such as the Periyar Tiger Reserve, Eravikulam National Park and Wayanad's wildlife sanctuaries have entry tickets and forest department rules, and some treks need permission. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations for travel within India. Drink bottled or filtered water, carry insect repellent and use sunscreen. In the monsoon Wayanad's forests have leeches, so wear closed shoes. Choose authorised centres for Ayurvedic treatments and tell them about any medical conditions. Carry your regular medicines.
travel_info.money: UPI and cards are widely accepted in towns, hotels and larger restaurants. Carry some cash for small shops, tea stalls, parking and tips, as ATMs are fewer in hill areas such as Munnar, Thekkady and Wayanad. Tipping drivers, houseboat crew and guides for good service is customary.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Kerala?
faqs.a: Four to five nights covers Munnar, Thekkady and the backwaters at a comfortable pace. Six to seven nights lets you add Kovalam or Varkala. A long weekend works for Kochi and an Alleppey houseboat.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Kerala?
faqs.a: November to March is dry and pleasant and is the main season. April and May are hot on the coast but fine in the hills. From June to September the monsoon is heavy, with lower prices, green scenery and some restrictions on travel and activities.

faqs.q: How do I reach Kerala from Chennai?
faqs.a: There are regular direct flights from Chennai to Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram, taking about an hour and a quarter. You can also take an overnight train to Ernakulam. Flights and trains are not included in our packages, but we can help you plan them.

faqs.q: Is Kerala suitable for senior parents and young children?
faqs.a: Yes. Most days are easy drives and boat rides. Some hill roads are winding, and a few sights such as Edakkal Caves involve steps or a climb, so tell us about any mobility needs and we will adjust the plan.

faqs.q: Can I get vegetarian or Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. Kerala has many vegetarian dishes, from sadhya to appam and stew. Jain meals can be requested in advance at hotels and houseboats, though the choice may be simpler in remote places.

faqs.q: Is an overnight houseboat stay worth it?
faqs.a: For most travellers it is the highlight of the trip. You cruise through the canals by day, moor at sunset and eat on board. Houseboats do not usually cruise at night, and space is shared with the crew, so it suits couples, families and small groups.

group_trips.title: Kerala Hills, Backwaters and Beaches Group Trip
group_trips.summary: Seven days in a small group through Fort Kochi, Munnar's tea hills, Periyar at Thekkady, an Alleppey houseboat night and the beaches of Kovalam.
group_trips.overview:
This fixed-departure group trip follows Kerala from the old port of Kochi, through the tea hills of Munnar and the forests of Thekkady, down to a night on a houseboat in Alleppey and a final stay by the sea at Kovalam. It covers the state's best-loved sights in seven days, with a trip captain to look after the group.

Drives are broken up with stops at waterfalls, spice plantations and viewpoints, and every day has some free time. Vegetarian and Indian meal options are available on request.

The group departs from Kochi and ends at Thiruvananthapuram, so you avoid a long drive back and can fly home from the airport nearest to Kovalam.
highlights: Fort Kochi's Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church and spice lanes
Munnar's tea plantations, Eravikulam National Park, Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point
Periyar Lake boat ride and spice plantation visit at Thekkady
Overnight stay on an Alleppey houseboat, with meals on board
Beach and lighthouse views at Kovalam

Overnight stay in Munnar.

itinerary.description:

itinerary.description:

Cruise the canals and Vembanad Lake in the afternoon, and enjoy dinner on board.

itinerary.description:

Overnight stay in Kovalam.

itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast and a last stroll by the sea.
Check out of the hotel.
Transfer to Thiruvananthapuram airport, about 30 to 40 minutes, for your journey home.

This weekend escape fits a night on the Alleppey backwaters and a day in Fort Kochi into three easy days. You land in Kochi early on Friday, drive to Alleppey for a houseboat cruise, then spend Saturday among the fishing nets, churches and spice lanes of Fort Kochi before an evening departure on Sunday.

It is short and relaxed, with one main activity each day. A trip captain travels with the group, and vegetarian and Indian meal options are available on request.

honeymoon_trips.title: Kerala Honeymoon: Munnar Mists, a Private Houseboat and Varkala Cliff
honeymoon_trips.summary: A private five-night honeymoon with misty Munnar, a night on a private Alleppey houseboat, a couples spa and a candlelight dinner above the sea at Varkala.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon moves from hills to water to sea over five nights. You begin in cool, misty Munnar among the tea plantations, then spend a night on a private houseboat in the Alleppey backwaters, and finish with two nights at Varkala, where the red cliff drops to the Arabian Sea.

Expect a flower welcome or bed decoration on arrival, a candlelight dinner at Varkala, a couples spa session and slow mornings with a private car and driver. All honeymoon touches are subject to availability. Tell us your wedding date at booking and we will pass it to the hotels.

Tea plantation views and Mattupetty Dam around Munnar
Overnight stay on a private Alleppey houseboat

custom_trips.title: Kerala Classic: Munnar Tea Hills, Periyar and Alleppey Houseboat
custom_trips.summary: Five nights through Kerala's best-loved circuit: Munnar's tea hills, Periyar wildlife at Thekkady, a night on an Alleppey houseboat and Fort Kochi.
custom_trips.overview:
This is Kerala's classic route in five nights, arranged as a private holiday with a car and driver. You start in the cool tea hills of Munnar, move on to the spice and forest country of Thekkady and spend a night afloat on the Alleppey backwaters.

The trip ends in Fort Kochi, where you can walk among the Chinese fishing nets, old churches and spice lanes before you fly or take the train home. It suits couples, families and first-time visitors who want the main sights without rushing.
highlights: Munnar's tea plantations, Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point
Eravikulam National Park, home of the Nilgiri tahr
Spice plantation visit and Periyar Lake boat ride at Thekkady
Overnight stay on an Alleppey houseboat, with meals on board
Fort Kochi's Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church and Jew Town
Private AC vehicle with driver for the whole route

itinerary.description:

Check in to your hotel and enjoy the cool evening air.
Overnight stay in Munnar.

itinerary.description:

Walk through the tea plantations and visit a tea museum.
Continue to Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point for lake and hill views.
Spend the evening at leisure.
Overnight stay in Munnar.

In the evening, attend an optional Kalaripayattu or Kathakali show, paid locally.
Overnight stay in Thekkady.

itinerary.title: Periyar Lake Boat Ride | Drive to Alleppey Houseboat
itinerary.description:
Take an early boat ride on Periyar Lake in the Periyar Tiger Reserve, subject to the reserve's schedule.
Drive to Alleppey, about four hours, and board your houseboat.
Cruise the canals and lake in the afternoon, passing village life and paddy fields.
Enjoy dinner on board as the boat moors for the night.
Overnight stay on the houseboat.

itinerary.title: Backwater Morning | Fort Kochi
itinerary.description:
Have breakfast on board and disembark by around 9 am.
Drive to Kochi, about two hours, and check in to your hotel.
Visit Fort Kochi: the Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church and the spice lanes of Jew Town.
Enjoy a sunset walk along the waterfront.
Overnight stay in Kochi.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kochi
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast and check out of the hotel.
Transfer to Cochin International Airport or Ernakulam railhead for your journey home.

custom_trips.title: Kerala Family Holiday: Munnar, Periyar Wildlife and Kumarakom Lake
custom_trips.summary: An easy-paced family holiday with Munnar's tea hills, a boat ride at Periyar and two relaxed nights by Vembanad Lake in Kumarakom.
custom_trips.overview:
This five-night private holiday keeps the driving manageable and the days varied, which suits families with children and grandparents. You see tea hills and a viewpoint-and-dam day in Munnar, watch for wildlife from a boat on Periyar Lake and end with two nights at a lakeside resort in Kumarakom.

The Kumarakom stay replaces the overnight houseboat with a daytime backwater cruise, so everyone sleeps on land and children can run about. Tell us your children's ages and we will suit the pace.
highlights: Tea plantations, Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point around Munnar
Eravikulam National Park with its Nilgiri tahr, if open
Periyar Lake boat ride and a spice plantation visit
Two nights at a lakeside stay in Kumarakom
Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary and a daytime backwater cruise
Private AC vehicle, with short driving days where possible

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kochi | Drive to Munnar
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Cochin International Airport or Ernakulam railhead, where your driver meets you.
Drive to Munnar, about four hours, with a break at a roadside waterfall.
Check in and rest, with the evening free.
Overnight stay in Munnar.

itinerary.title: Munnar Tea Hills | Mattupetty Dam | Echo Point
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Eravikulam National Park, subject to it being open.
Walk through a tea plantation and see how tea is made at a tea museum.
Stop at Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point, with optional boating paid locally.
Free evening.
Overnight stay in Munnar.

itinerary.title: Munnar to Thekkady | Spice Plantation
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Thekkady, about four hours.
Visit a spice plantation and learn how pepper, cardamom and vanilla grow.
Spend the evening at leisure, or attend an optional cultural show paid locally.
Overnight stay in Thekkady.

itinerary.title: Periyar Lake Boat Ride | Drive to Kumarakom
itinerary.description:
Take a boat ride on Periyar Lake in the Periyar Tiger Reserve, subject to the reserve's schedule.
Drive to Kumarakom, about four hours, and check in to your lakeside stay.
Relax by the water for the rest of the day.
Overnight stay in Kumarakom.

itinerary.title: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary | Backwater Cruise
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary for a gentle walk among the birds and trees.
Enjoy a daytime cruise on Vembanad Lake and the nearby canals.
Spend the evening at leisure at the resort.
Overnight stay in Kumarakom.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kochi
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Drive to Cochin International Airport or Ernakulam railhead, about two and a half hours, for your journey home.

custom_trips.title: Wayanad Wilds: Caves, Waterfalls and Forest Trails
custom_trips.summary: Four nights in the Western Ghats of Wayanad, with Edakkal Caves, Banasura Sagar, waterfalls, spice gardens and optional forest and wildlife activities.
custom_trips.overview:
Wayanad is Kerala's quieter hill district, with forests, tea and spice estates, lakes and waterfalls. This four-night private trip bases you in the district and visits Banasura Sagar Dam, Pookode Lake, the prehistoric carvings at Edakkal Caves and the Soochipara Falls, with room for easy walks.

It suits friends, young travellers and families who enjoy being outdoors. Some of the activities involve steps or a short climb, and forest trails and safaris are subject to forest department rules and the weather. We quote this trip on request, so tell us your dates and group size.
highlights: Edakkal Caves and their ancient rock carvings, reached by a stepped climb
Banasura Sagar Dam and its island-dotted reservoir
Soochipara Falls, with a walk down to the pool when conditions allow
Pookode Lake and spice and tea estate views
Optional wildlife safari or forest trek, subject to forest department rules
Private AC vehicle with driver throughout

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kozhikode | Drive to Wayanad
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Calicut International Airport or Kozhikode railhead, where your driver meets you.
Drive up to Wayanad, about three hours, through the winding Thamarassery ghat road.
Check in to your hotel or resort and relax.
Overnight stay in Wayanad.

itinerary.title: Pookode Lake | Banasura Sagar Dam
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Pookode Lake, a freshwater lake set in forest.
Continue to Banasura Sagar Dam for views of the reservoir and hills.
Spend the evening at leisure or take a short walk through a spice and coffee estate.
Overnight stay in Wayanad.

itinerary.title: Edakkal Caves | Spice Gardens
itinerary.description:
Drive to Edakkal Caves and climb the steps to see the ancient carvings on the rock walls.
Visit a spice garden to see pepper, cardamom and coffee growing.
Enjoy the afternoon at leisure, or add a forest safari, paid locally and subject to availability.
Overnight stay in Wayanad.

itinerary.title: Soochipara Falls | Forest Trail
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Soochipara Falls and walk down to view the waterfall, subject to the water level.
Take an easy forest trail with a local guide where permitted.
Return to the hotel for a free evening.
Overnight stay in Wayanad.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kozhikode
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast and check out of the hotel.
Drive to Calicut International Airport or Kozhikode railhead, about three hours, for your journey home.
